location.en: Maple Bay Career Fair, Harbor Convention Center
location.zh: 楓灣就業博覽會，港灣會議中心

goal.en: Pitch yourself to recruiters and leave your resume at a booth you like.
goal.zh: 向招募人員推銷自己，並在喜歡的攤位留下履歷。

background: large convention hall with rows of company booths, blank display boards, tables with stacks of brochures with blank covers, carpeted aisles, bright overhead lights, daytime

intro.en: The Maple Bay Career Fair is packed. You hold a folder of freshly printed resumes and take a deep breath.
intro.zh: 楓灣就業博覽會人潮洶湧。你抱著一疊剛印好的履歷，深吸一口氣。

intro.en: Your working holiday visa lets you work, and now it is time to find a real job.
intro.zh: 你的打工度假簽證可以合法工作，現在該找份正式的工作了。

lines.en: Hi there! Welcome to the Harbor Grand Hotel booth. What kind of work are you looking for?
lines.zh: 嗨！歡迎來到港灣大飯店的攤位。你在找什麼樣的工作？

choices.en: I'm interested in marketing or customer service roles.
choices.zh: 我對行銷或客服類的職位有興趣。
choices.tip: I'm interested in + 名詞或 V-ing，清楚說出想找的方向。

choices.en: I'm interesting in marketing or customer service jobs.
choices.zh: 我對行銷或客服工作很有興趣。

lines.en: You're interesting? Well, I'm sure you are! But what job do you want?
lines.zh: 你很有趣？嗯，我相信你很有趣！但你想找什麼工作？

story.en: The recruiter laughs politely and turns to the next visitor. You walk away still wondering what was so funny.
story.zh: 招募人員客氣地笑了笑，轉頭招呼下一位訪客。你走開時還在想到底哪裡好笑。

fail.why: interesting 是「令人覺得有趣」，interested 才是「感到有興趣」。說自己對某事有興趣要用 I'm interested in...，說 I'm interesting 等於在誇自己很有趣。

choices.en: Any job is okay. I can eat bitter, no problem!
choices.zh: 什麼工作都可以，我很能吃苦，沒問題！

lines.en: Eat... bitter? Is that a kind of food?
lines.zh: 吃……苦的東西？那是一種食物嗎？

story.en: The recruiter thinks you want a kitchen job tasting bitter melon soup. Not quite the career you had in mind.
story.zh: 招募人員以為你想進飯店廚房，負責試喝苦瓜湯。這不太是你想要的職涯。

fail.why: 「吃苦」直譯成 eat bitter，英文母語者聽不懂。想表達肯努力，說 I'm a hard worker. 或 I don't mind hard work.；「什麼工作都可以」也聽起來沒有方向，最好說出具體的興趣。

lines.en: Hmm, right now we mostly need night-shift kitchen staff. But Brightway, two booths down, is hiring people with language skills.
lines.zh: 嗯，我們現在主要缺夜班廚房人員。不過往前兩個攤位的 Brightway 正在找有語言能力的人。

choices.en: Kitchen? No way. That job is too low for me.
choices.zh: 廚房？才不要，那種工作太低階了。

lines.en: Our kitchen team works very hard, you know.
lines.zh: 我們的廚房團隊可是很辛苦的。

story.en: The recruiter's smile freezes. Lesson learned: every booth at a career fair is someone's whole team.
story.zh: 招募人員的笑容瞬間凍結。學到一課：博覽會上每個攤位，背後都是一整個團隊。

fail.why: 看不起別人的職缺，會讓對方覺得被冒犯。不感興趣時客氣婉拒即可：That's not quite what I'm looking for, but thank you.。

choices.en: That sounds like a great fit. Thanks for the tip!
choices.zh: 聽起來很適合我，謝謝你的建議！
choices.tip: Thanks for the tip! 是感謝別人提供資訊的自然說法。

choices.en: I love nights! I usually go to bed really late, haha.
choices.zh: 我超愛晚上！我平常都很晚才睡，哈哈。

lines.en: Oh... okay. So you're applying for the night shift, then?
lines.zh: 喔……好喔。所以你是要應徵夜班囉？

story.en: Before you know it, your name is on the night-shift list. Brightway's booth fades into the crowd behind you.
story.zh: 回過神來，你的名字已經在夜班名單上了。Brightway 的攤位消失在人潮裡。

fail.why: 對方是在介紹另一個機會，你卻扯到自己的作息，聽起來像在應徵夜班。聽到推薦時先道謝：Thanks for the tip! I'll go check it out.。

lines.en: At the Brightway booth, a few warm lamps glow on the table. A woman with a tablet looks up.
lines.zh: Brightway 的攤位上，幾盞暖色檯燈亮著。一位拿著平板的女士抬起頭。

lines.en: Hi, I'm Rachel from Brightway. We make smart lighting for hotels, cafés and offices. Tell me a bit about yourself.
lines.zh: 嗨，我是 Brightway 的瑞秋。我們做智慧照明，客戶有飯店、咖啡店和辦公室。跟我說說你自己吧。

choices.en: My name is Kai. My English is not good, and I don't really have experience. Sorry.
choices.zh: 我叫凱。我的英文不好，也沒什麼經驗，不好意思。

lines.en: Oh... your English sounds fine to me. But then, why should we hire you?
lines.zh: 喔……我覺得你的英文聽起來沒問題啊。不過，那我們為什麼要錄取你？

story.en: Rachel nods kindly but writes nothing down. Modesty is polite in Taiwan, but at a career fair, it hides everything good about you.
story.zh: 瑞秋親切地點點頭，卻什麼也沒寫下。謙虛在台灣是禮貌，但在博覽會上，它把你的優點全藏起來了。

fail.why: 在台灣先自謙是禮貌，但在求職場合，對方會照字面相信你「英文不好、沒經驗」。要聚焦在自己能做的事：I've done customer service, and I speak Chinese and English.。

choices.en: I'm Kai from Taiwan. I've done customer service, and I speak Chinese and English.
choices.zh: 我是來自台灣的凱。我做過客服，會說中文和英文。
choices.tip: 30 秒自我推銷：名字＋相關經驗＋能為對方帶來的能力。

choices.en: I'm Kai. I'm 22, I'm single, I love bubble tea and my blood type is O.
choices.zh: 我是凱，22 歲，單身，喜歡珍奶，血型 O 型。

lines.en: Ha, good to know... but how does that help with the job?
lines.zh: 哈，知道了……不過這跟工作有什麼關係？

story.en: Rachel learns your blood type, but nothing about your skills. She hands you a candy and politely wishes you luck.
story.zh: 瑞秋知道了你的血型，卻對你的能力一無所知。她遞給你一顆糖，客氣地祝你好運。

fail.why: 求職自介要講和工作有關的經驗與能力。年齡、感情狀態、血型都跟職缺無關，在很多國家也不該在求職時主動提起。

lines.en: That's great. We're actually looking for a sales and marketing assistant. Do you have any questions about the position?
lines.zh: 很好。我們正好在找業務行銷助理。你對這個職位有什麼問題嗎？

choices.en: Yes. What kind of skills are you looking for?
choices.zh: 有的。你們在找具備什麼能力的人？
choices.tip: What kind of skills are you looking for? 是在博覽會上了解職缺的好問題。

choices.en: Yes. How much is the salary, and how many days off?
choices.zh: 有，薪水多少？休假有幾天？

lines.en: Well... we usually discuss that much later in the process.
lines.zh: 嗯……那個通常會在很後面的流程才談。

story.en: Rachel's smile gets a little stiff. Your first question about the job was about money, and she makes a small note on her tablet.
story.zh: 瑞秋的笑容有點僵。你對這份工作的第一個問題是錢，她在平板上默默記了一筆。

fail.why: 第一次接觸就問薪水和休假，會讓人覺得你只在乎待遇。博覽會上先問工作內容：What kind of skills are you looking for?，薪資留到面試後段或對方提起再談。

choices.en: Yes. Can you explain me more about this job?
choices.zh: 有，你可以跟我多解釋一下這份工作嗎？

lines.en: Explain... you? Oh, you mean explain the job to you. Sure.
lines.zh: 解釋……你？喔，你是說跟你解釋這份工作。好啊。

story.en: Rachel figures it out, but the confusion eats up your short time at the booth. A long line has already formed behind you.
story.zh: 瑞秋最後聽懂了，但剛才的混亂用掉了你在攤位前寶貴的時間，後面已經排了一長串人。

fail.why: explain 後面不能直接接人。要說 Could you explain the job to me? 或 Could you tell me more about the job?。

lines.en: We'd love to hear from you. Is there anything else I can help you with?
lines.zh: 我們很期待你的消息。還有什麼我可以幫忙的嗎？

choices.en: Please give me a chance! I will work very hard!
choices.zh: 請給我一個機會！我會很努力！

lines.en: Oh! Um, well, the first step is just sending your resume.
lines.zh: 喔！呃，第一步其實只是投履歷而已。

story.en: Rachel looks a little uncomfortable. You meant to sound eager, but you sounded like your life depended on it.
story.zh: 瑞秋看起來有點不自在。你想表現積極，聽起來卻像攸關生死。

fail.why: 「請給我一個機會」直接講出來，在英文裡聽起來像在哀求，反而讓對方有壓力。用具體行動表達興趣：Could I leave my resume with you?。

choices.en: Can I throw my resume here? I printed many copies.
choices.zh: 我可以在這裡投履歷嗎？我印了很多份。

lines.en: Throw it? Please don't throw anything at me!
lines.zh: 丟過來？拜託不要丟東西給我！

story.en: Rachel ducks behind her tablet, laughing. You hand it over gently, but the booth staff call you 'the thrower' all afternoon.
story.zh: 瑞秋笑著躲到平板後面。你改成輕輕遞過去，但整個下午攤位的人都叫你「丟履歷的人」。

fail.why: 中文的「投履歷」不能直譯成 throw，throw 是真的「丟」。英文說 send 或 submit my resume，當面遞交則說 Could I leave my resume with you?。

choices.en: Could I leave my resume with you?
choices.zh: 我可以把履歷留給你嗎？
choices.tip: Could I leave my resume with you? 是博覽會上遞履歷最得體的說法。

lines.en: Rachel slips your resume into her folder and hands you a business card.
lines.zh: 瑞秋把你的履歷收進資料夾，遞給你一張名片。

lines.en: Of course! I'll pass it to our manager, Ms. Wong. Expect a call from us soon.
lines.zh: 當然！我會轉交給我們的王經理。請等我們的電話。

story.en: You leave the fair with a business card in your pocket and a good feeling about Brightway.
story.zh: 你離開博覽會時，口袋裡多了一張名片，心裡對 Brightway 有種好預感。

notes.explain: 說明求職方向的基本句型，後面接名詞或 V-ing。注意是 interested，不是 interesting。

example.en: I'm interested in working with international clients.
example.zh: 我對和國際客戶合作有興趣。

notes.en: I've done customer service, and I speak two languages.
notes.zh: 我做過客服，也會說兩種語言。
notes.explain: 30 秒自我推銷：名字＋一項相關經驗＋一項能力。用現在完成式 I've done、I've worked 帶出經驗。

example.en: I'm Kai. I've worked at a café, and I'm good with people.
example.zh: 我是凱，在咖啡店工作過，很會跟人相處。

notes.en: Could I leave my resume with you?
notes.zh: 我可以把履歷留給你嗎？
notes.explain: 博覽會或店面當面遞履歷的標準問法。投遞履歷則說 send 或 submit my resume，不要用 throw。

example.en: I'd like to submit my resume for the assistant position.
example.zh: 我想投遞履歷應徵助理職位。

notes.zh: 令人覺得有趣 vs. 感到有興趣
notes.explain: -ing 形容詞描述「帶給別人的感覺」，-ed 形容詞描述「自己的感受」。I'm interesting 是在說自己很有趣。

example.en: The job sounds interesting. I'm very interested.
example.zh: 這份工作聽起來很有趣，我很有興趣。

notes.en: Skip the salary talk at first.
notes.explain: 博覽會是建立第一印象的地方，先問工作內容和需要的能力。也別自謙說英文不好，對方會照字面相信。

example.en: What kind of skills are you looking for?
example.zh: 你們在找具備什麼能力的人？
